note: IRR adjudication metadata. Separate from reports/p2004_irr_metrics_v1.json, whose raw pre-adjudication reliability figures are unchanged.

not_obligation_rule.settled_rule: Treat a span as an obligation when it states a complete mandatory compliance condition that the regulated entity must ensure, even when phrased passively or as a mandatory condition on a document or process. Mark not_obligation only when the span is incomplete, purely definitional, scope-setting only, classification-only, merely illustrative or a worked example, or clearly assigns the duty to a non-regulated third party.

rejected.rationale: Reject: the extracted text ends at 'develop an exit strategy that shall' and contains no complete operative requirement to annotate.
Reject: this is a criterion describing when an outsourced activity is critical/material, not a duty requiring an RE to perform an action.
Reject: the paragraph is a dated worked illustration of SMA/NPA tagging, not the general operative classification rule itself.
Reject: this paragraph only defines which amalgamation cases fall within the Directions; it is a scope/applicability clause, not an operative duty.
Reject: the USD 2 million statement is the numerical result in a worked example, not a standalone obligation imposed on the SFB.

kept_as_obligation.rationale: Keep as an obligation: the one-month age limit is an operative compliance condition the AIFI must ensure; Commercial Banks have the same rule with a six-month limit.
Keep as an obligation: passive audit wording still creates a control the RRB must ensure; UCB has the exact valuation-at-audit rule and SFB only a broader audit-control rule.
Keep as an obligation because the paragraph identifies 'A SFB' as the actor; PB/RCB alert rules overlap in customer communication but do not match the full deposit-proof/statement duties.

not_obligation_rule.support: Supported by the adjudicated decisions: every rejection is an incomplete span, a classification/criterion-only clause, a worked example or a scope clause, and every overturned rejection vote was a complete mandatory condition (including passive wording). No disputed item here was rejected as purely definitional or as a third-party duty; those two clauses rest on guidelines v1 and v2.1, not on this adjudication.
